items.headline: Qunova's hybrid method matches the best classical result on a hard chemistry problem
items.summary: Qunova Computing says its HI-VQE algorithm reached chemical accuracy in an 80-qubit simulation of the 4Fe-4S iron-sulfur cluster, using an IBM Quantum System Two machine at RIKEN alongside the Fugaku supercomputer. Its ground-state energy estimate of minus 327.2482 Hartree agreed within chemical accuracy with the leading classical reference, calculated by the Density Matrix Renormalization Group method at minus 327.2471 Hartree. The workflow also used about 300 times fewer Fugaku node-hours than a previously published sample-based quantum diagonalization approach on the same molecule.
items.why: A quantum workflow that agrees with the reference classical calculation on a benchmark molecule gives chemists a reason to trust hybrid methods for real design questions.

items.headline: AWS upgrades its AgentCore runtime for faster, cheaper agent sessions
items.summary: Amazon Web Services has released a new version of the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, the managed layer that runs AI agents in isolated Firecracker micro virtual machines. Sessions now start up to 15 times faster and scale to four times more compute, up to 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of memory, while idle sessions scale to zero and reclaim memory within minutes. Agents can also mount storage such as an S3 bucket inside the session boundary, so data stays under the same controls as the compute.
items.why: Agents that run for hours need isolation that does not tax every minute of waiting, and this release ties billing and storage to how agents actually work.

items.headline: Chainguard defends shipping PHP patches six hours before the agreed release time
items.summary: Chainguard has defended its decision to publish patched PHP container images at 07:41 UTC on October 21, six hours and 19 minutes before the agreed 14:00 UTC coordinated release for the critical PHP2Shell flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Chief technology officer Matt Moore told KubeCon that attackers already had a head start, pointing to leaked vulnerability details, a mistakenly published proof-of-concept video, a honeypot exploitation attempt reported by Amazon on October 17, and attack traffic seen by Cloudflare. PHP said it found no working public exploit at release time, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26.
items.why: Coordinated disclosure only works when everyone holds the line, so an early release by one vendor forces the whole industry to rethink how embargoes are enforced.

items.headline: Apache patches a critical HTTP/2 flaw that allows remote code execution
items.summary: The Apache Software Foundation has fixed a critical race condition in the mod_http2 module of Apache HTTP Server, tracked as CVE-2026-119618, which an unauthenticated attacker could exploit to gain remote code execution. The flaw affects HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and was found by Anthropic's OSS Scanner and Google Cloud's Vulnerability Research teams. Cloud security company Wiz reports that 64% of cloud environments hold vulnerable resources, though the flaw needs HTTP/2 enabled, which is off by default, and no public exploit is known.
items.why: Apache still serves about one in five websites, so a remotely exploitable flaw in its HTTP/2 code is a patch-now item for anyone running it.

items.headline: New SignDrop zero-day turns a Windows security mitigation into a privilege escalation
items.summary: Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri has disclosed SignDrop, a Windows zero-day that abuses the Common Log File System mitigations Microsoft added in October 2025. The flaw lets an attacker trick a privileged process, such as an antivirus engine, into creating an authentication file with SYSTEM privileges, which can then be used to turn off antivirus and endpoint protection. Naceri tested the exploit on Windows 11 26H2 and Windows Server 2025 Experimental, estimates 80% of Windows installations are vulnerable, and says there is no fix yet except waiting for a Microsoft patch.
items.why: A defence that can be turned against itself is a reminder that mitigations need their own review, and defenders cannot patch this one yet.

items.headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigns; finance chief Colette Kress takes over on an interim basis
items.summary: Nvidia has announced that Jensen Huang has resigned as president, chief executive officer and a member of the board, effective immediately, ending 33 years as chief executive of the company he co-founded in 1993. The announcement gave no reason for the departure, which followed days of reports about Huang's personal conduct and a board investigation, while chief financial officer Colette Kress takes over as interim chief executive and the board searches for a permanent successor. The board also named longtime director Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever chair, and Nvidia confirmed its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results will still be reported on November 17 as scheduled.
items.why: A change at the top of the chipmaker at the centre of the AI buildout will shape chip supply, pricing and US export policy debates.

items.headline: Q-CTRL raises $290 million and becomes the quantum sector's newest unicorn
items.summary: Q-CTRL has raised US$290 million in a Series C round led by Salesforce Ventures, with participation from Bullhound Capital and Affinity Partners, reaching unicorn status. The oversubscribed round was expanded twice to meet investor demand, and the company says it is the largest fundraise for a software-focused quantum business. Q-CTRL plans to use the money to expand globally, strengthen its AI-powered quantum software, and scale customer programs in finance, energy, autonomy and aerospace, including its Ironstone Opal navigation system that works without GPS.
items.why: Private money is concentrating on the software layer that makes quantum hardware usable, and a round of this size signals where investors expect value to sit.

items.headline: Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot worldwide
items.summary: Microsoft is investigating a widespread Microsoft 365 outage that began on Thursday at 1:26 PM ET and left customers unable to connect to Outlook, Teams, SharePoint Online, Copilot and Defender XDR. Microsoft said the disruption was caused by servers unexpectedly becoming unavailable, which strained the remaining infrastructure, and it has paused deployments, redistributed traffic and begun restarting servers. By Thursday evening Microsoft reported limited recovery after returning some servers to service, but had not confirmed when services would be fully restored.
items.why: A single outage that takes out mail, chat and AI assistance at once shows how much daily work now depends on one provider's infrastructure.

items.headline: Blacklisted Chinese university bought Nvidia H200 chips despite US export controls
items.summary: A Reuters investigation of procurement records found that Northwestern Polytechnical University in China bought two Nvidia H200 AI chips for 874,700 yuan, about $123,000, on October 21, through Chinese supplier Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology rather than directly from Nvidia. The university has been on the US Entity List since 2001 over missile-proliferation and military research concerns, and Reuters reviewed 26 records showing Chinese institutions buying restricted Nvidia chips or renting computing capacity through domestic suppliers. The US has allowed some H200 exports to China on a case-by-case basis since January, with safeguards against blacklisted and military end users, and Nvidia, the university and the US Commerce Department did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment.
items.why: The purchase shows how export controls are tested in practice, through intermediaries and rentals, and the gap between the rules and enforcement is now part of the policy debate.

items.headline: ChatGPT Wallet lets agents pay without seeing your card details
items.summary: OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Wallet, a way for its Dots agents to pay for purchases on a user's behalf without seeing the user's actual card details. Users add a card once and approve each purchase with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint, after which the payment network issues a token in place of the real card number. The wallet starts with ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US, built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, and OpenAI has published a Commerce Partner Playbook to help businesses accept agent payments.
items.why: Agent-led shopping only works if payments are safe and merchants can accept them, so a wallet built on existing card rails is the missing piece for agentic commerce.

items.headline: Anthropic opens a private beta for self-hosted Claude Managed Agents
items.summary: Anthropic has opened a private beta of self-hosted Claude Managed Agents, letting companies run the whole agent service inside their own cloud or data centre. The harness, sandboxes, credentials and session history all run on the customer's infrastructure, while model calls still go to a provider the customer chooses, such as Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google's Agent Platform or Microsoft Foundry. Access is limited to eligible organisations through their Anthropic account team, and the server licence requires customers to roll back a version within eight hours of a safety notice.
items.why: Teams that want long-running agents working on internal code can now keep the control plane behind their own security perimeter instead of handing it to a vendor.

items.headline: llama.cpp reaches 1.0 with a stability promise for local AI builders
items.summary: The llama.cpp project has released version 1.0.0 of its libraries, committing to semantic versioning so that breaking changes to the public C API will only arrive with major version bumps. The project, which lets developers run multimodal language models on hardware from consumer laptops to enterprise servers, now supports more than 150 model architecture variants. The release also covers ggml 1.0.0, the tensor library underneath it.
items.why: Local and private AI products depend on llama.cpp, so a stable API gives their builders a firmer foundation to build on.

items.headline: Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN and IBM simulate drug binding across 12,000 atoms
items.summary: A collaboration between Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN and IBM has run a hybrid quantum-classical simulation of full protein-ligand complexes exceeding 12,000 atoms, described as the largest such calculation to date. The team paired two 156-qubit IBM Heron r2 processors with three supercomputers, collecting 3.0 billion measurement shots across 21,006 circuits, and reported up to a 210-fold improvement in fragment energy accuracy over earlier quantum-embedding benchmarks. The work, detailed in a preprint, produced a binding energy prediction for a T4-lysozyme complex.
items.why: Drug binding predictions at this scale move quantum computing closer to real pharmaceutical work, where accurate energies decide which molecules advance.

items.headline: A cheaper way to hunt for diamond qubits
items.summary: A researcher at the US Department of Energy's Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory has developed a method that cuts the cost of modelling quantum defects in diamond, by treating a cluster of just 16 to 30 atoms around a defect as a separate molecule. The approach, published in ACS Central Science, already identified promising new qubit candidates involving boron and oxygen defects, which emit ultraviolet and blue light respectively, unlike the well-known nitrogen-vacancy centre that emits red. Because each defect type responds to different light, several kinds could be combined in one device and addressed independently.
items.why: Cheaper screening of diamond defects widens the search for qubits that work at room temperature, which would simplify quantum hardware.

items.headline: Google Cloud brings agentic HPC to SC26
items.summary: Google Cloud has set out its agentic high-performance computing plans for the SC26 supercomputing conference, centred on reusable agent skills that teach AI agents to build and run HPC workloads through Cluster Toolkit blueprints. The skills validate quotas and capacity before deploying a cluster, guide domain work such as fluid dynamics and life-science pipelines, and operate inside IAM and budget guardrails. The company is also showing AlphaEvolve on Cloud Batch for evolving code at scale, and new hardware including A5X instances on NVIDIA Vera Rubin and 8th generation TPUs.
items.why: Scientific teams are asking agents to run supercomputing workloads, so packaging HPC expertise into skills keeps those agents from misconfiguring expensive infrastructure.

items.headline: Check Point zero-day chained with PHP2Shell to wipe VMware hosts
items.summary: Check Point has released emergency hotfixes for a zero-day privilege escalation flaw, CVE-2026-123039, that attackers have exploited against a couple of dozen customers since late October. Attackers first entered through Mobile Access portals using the PHP2Shell flaws, then used the flaw to run commands as root, installed the TSGA backdoor, and in an early wave wiped VMware ESXi hosts. The company advises customers who cannot patch immediately to stop the DynamicCLI daemon as a temporary mitigation.
items.why: A chained portal flaw plus a root escalation shows how one unpatched gateway can become a route to destructive attacks on virtualisation hosts.

items.headline: FBI says North Korean hackers stole over $400 million in deepfake video call scheme
items.summary: The FBI says North Korean hackers stole more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over 18 months through a scheme it calls FaceStealer, which lures targets into fake video meetings that play recorded webcam footage of people they trust. Once on the call, victims are told of a fake audio fault and sent a link that installs malware to steal wallets and credentials. US authorities seized the cloud infrastructure behind the scheme and more than 900 recorded victim videos, and the Justice Department separately won court approval to seize or restrain over $1.2 billion stolen from Binance by a different North Korean group.
items.why: The scheme turns a victim's own face into the lure for the next target, so verifying meeting invitations through a second channel matters more than ever.

items.headline: Operation Endgame seizes servers behind Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC
items.summary: An international police operation has taken down servers behind the Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC malware tools, seizing 235 servers and 257 domains and about 6.4 million stolen logins belonging to more than 40,000 victims. Gootloader spread through fake legal documents on hacked websites and was used in ransomware attacks, while CastleRAT gave attackers remote control of infected machines and StealC stole passwords. Dutch police have loaded data stolen by CastleRAT into their Check your hack service so people can see if their email address was affected.
items.why: Taking down the loaders and stealers that feed ransomware cuts off the access brokers' supply chain, even when no arrests are announced.

items.headline: Trezor confirms hardware implants in three wallets and cuts reseller network
items.summary: Trezor has confirmed that three Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained hidden circuit boards designed to steal recovery phrases and send them to attackers over a mobile network. The company released firmware 2.13.1 on November 11, which stops the implants from capturing anything on screen, and says no affected customer has reported losing funds. Trezor has also cut its global reseller network by about 80 percent and is offering replacement devices to anyone who bought a wallet from CryptoBilis since March 2026.
items.why: A hardware wallet is only as trustworthy as its supply chain, so a tampered device shows why buying from authorised sellers matters.

items.headline: Atom Computing finalises $100 million Commerce Department award
items.summary: Atom Computing has signed an agreement for up to $100 million with the US Department of Commerce to accelerate research and development of fault-tolerant, utility-scale quantum computers built on neutral atoms. The award, made under the CHIPS and Science Act, follows a letter of intent announced earlier in 2026 and will fund in-house technology work, expanded engineering and testing infrastructure, and supply chain collaboration. Atom also recently advanced to Stage C of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, with potential funding of up to $300 million.
items.why: Federal funding at this scale signals that neutral-atom quantum computing is now treated as strategic infrastructure, not just research.

items.headline: Operation TorNado arrests 354 in global dark web crackdown
items.summary: Police in 14 countries have arrested 354 people and seized more than $234 million in cash and virtual currencies in Operation TorNado, a coordinated action against vendors and buyers on five dark web marketplaces that had already been seized by law enforcement. The operation, which ran from May 2025 to October 2026, also seized about 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs, 209 firearms and 38 pill presses. The US Justice Department, which announced the results with Europol, said 132 of the arrests were in the United States.
items.why: Seized marketplaces keep producing leads, so each takedown feeds the next round of arrests rather than ending the trade.
